items.title: A 6-person startup's loop beat Gemini 3 Deep Think on ARC-AGI-2
items.why: No bigger model, just generate-critique-refine-verify over Gemini 3 Pro — open source, cheaper too.

items.title: Karpathy says he now writes code mostly in English, not syntax
items.why: His shift: describe intent, let agents draft, review hard, cut the bloat they tend to leave behind.

items.title: Someone packed a full AI agent into 140MB, running on a Pi Zero
items.why: 35 providers, 72 tools, a task queue — open source and light enough for a $15 board.

items.title: The LHC's new magnets hit 12 tesla, and the trick is a brittle metal
items.why: Niobium-tin beats niobium-titanium but shatters if wound wrong — a real materials tradeoff, not just a bigger number.

items.title: Rust's decade-long trait solver rewrite is finally landing
items.why: It's the engine behind every generic bound check in the compiler; specialization fixes may follow it.

items.title: Go's new default GC scans memory in neighborhoods, not scattered
items.why: Better cache locality cut one team's GC pauses by a third with zero code changes — worth checking on your own service.

items.title: A one-liner to catch which process is hammering your syscalls
items.why: bpftrace on raw_syscalls finds chatty polling loops in about ten seconds — keep it in your back pocket.

items.title: A prefix-sum-plus-hashing trick for counting special subarrays fast
items.why: Turns an O(n^2) subarray scan into O(n) — useful next time a CF problem smells like a hashing trick.

items.title: Dopamine may work like a GPS, not just a reward signal
items.why: A real-time course-correction signal, separate from reward — interesting, but its link to focus is still unproven.

items.title: A blood protein tracked who kept their muscle over four years
items.why: Association only, but it backs what already works: keep lifting and spread protein across meals, not just dinner.
items.source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle (via mindbodygreen)
